title: Puntland Maritime Police Rescue Sanctioned Tanker Sibu 1, Capture Dozens of Pirates
detail: The Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) and Puntland Navy freed the US-sanctioned tanker Sibu 1 (formerly Seamull) off the coast of Mudug region on September 25, 2026, concluding a 48-hour pursuit and assault operation. One pirate was killed and four to five were wounded in the raid; reporting on the number of suspects taken into custody ranges from 15 (Dawan Africa's initial count of those captured in the final assault) to 41-42 (broader totals cited by Arab News and US News, likely including earlier-detained accomplices ashore); one Puntland police officer was injured. All 20 crew members — reported by Dawan Africa as 16 Indian, 2 Syrian, 1 Iraqi and 1 Sudanese nationals — were confirmed safe along with the vessel's cargo. Sibu 1 had been seized by six armed pirates approximately 136 nautical miles east of Al Mukalla, Yemen, on August 20, 2026, and steered toward Somalia's Puntland coast; the US Treasury sanctioned the vessel in December 2025 for allegedly carrying Iranian 'shadow fleet' petroleum products in violation of sanctions. It is the first Puntland-led armed recovery of a hijacked vessel in the 2026 piracy resurgence — a different resolution path than the ransom-based release of the cargo vessel Sword around September 11. Three other hijacked tankers — Honour 25, MT Eureka, and the previously unreported MT Asana (a Tanzanian-flagged tanker seized off Yemen around July 17 with roughly 20 crew, including German and Filipino nationals, and taken to Puntland's Bari region) — remain in pirate hands, reportedly relocated south toward Hobyo, Galmudug.

media.caption: Puntland Maritime Police Force says all 20 crew of the sanctioned tanker MT Sibu 1 are safe after a 48-hour rescue operation, Sep 25, 2026
The tanker Sibu 1 (Seamull), rescued off Somalia's Mudug coast after a 48-hour Puntland Maritime Police operation

title: Mohamud's UN Pledge of 'Universal Suffrage' Draws Opposition Backlash Over Term Extension
detail: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's September 24, 2026 address to the UN General Assembly's 81st session general debate — in which he said 'through constitutional reform, we're laying the foundations of universal suffrage, accountable institutions and a multi-party system that allows every Somali citizen to have a voice' — drew sharp domestic criticism reported September 25, 2026, amid Somalia's ongoing constitutional dispute. Mohamud's original four-year term expired May 15, 2026; he has continued governing under a disputed 'transition period' following March 2026 parliamentary amendments — which he signed — extending presidential and parliamentary terms to five years and pushing elections to 2027. Former Presidents Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo and Sheikh Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, along with the Puntland and Jubaland state administrations, have rejected the amendments as passed without required consensus; critics said Mohamud should have resolved the domestic political crisis before touting democratic reform abroad, and noted Somalia still lacks the updated electoral registry and infrastructure needed for genuine one-person-one-vote elections. The dispute has previously produced violence, including the June 3-5, 2026 Mogadishu urban warfare between government and opposition-aligned forces.

media.caption: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's UN pledge of 'universal suffrage' draws opposition criticism amid the term-extension dispute, Sep 25, 2026
